name: CA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 district with a well-funded Democratic incumbent
Challenger Littau shows no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%
No public polling; the margin rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Huffman pairs a strongly Democratic North Coast district with a roughly $1 million fundraising edge over a challenger who has raised essentially nothing, and markets price the race near 98% Democratic. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the seat stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: Without polling, the only realistic signal of movement would be a late surge in challenger fundraising or outside spending, neither of which is currently visible.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 2nd District leans Democratic by about 13 points, and Democrat Jared Huffman is the incumbent on the November ballot against Republican Robin Littau. Huffman enters the general election with roughly $1.1 million on hand after raising nearly $1 million, while Littau shows no reported fundraising and outside spending in the race is negligible. No public polls cover the contest, and no expert raters have listed it.

Prediction markets put Huffman's chances near 98 percent, and the fundamentals point the same way: the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial advantage, and a challenger with little visible campaign activity. The expected margin sits in the low twenties, wide enough to rate the seat Safe Democratic. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves the precise margin loose but does not change the likely outcome.
